Remove outliers, now this is the dataset we want to use: 
```{r}
df1 <- df %>% 
  filter(!(species %in% c("QUEAGR") & date %in% c("2022-04-27") & study %in% c("Sedgwick"))) %>% 
  mutate(study_nice = case_when(
    study %in% c("Pepperwood") ~ "PwD",
    study %in% c("Sedgwick") ~ "SeR",
    study %in% c("SEKI") ~ "PrC",
    study %in% c("StuntRanch") ~ "StR"
  ))
# SEKI keeps new, old and mixed tissue together: field fuels are a mix of current and
# previous years' growth (see Discussion). A new-tissue-only filter was used Feb–Oct 2026.

df1 %>% 
  write_csv(here("data", "df1.csv"))
  

unique(df1$study)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Hybrid Psi-min per species:
#   - EVT POT-GPD Psi-min when tail sample large enough
#   - Observed minimum otherwise
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(fExtremes)

# --- Load ---
dat <- df1 %>%
  mutate(
    mwp = as.numeric(mwp),
    psi_abs = abs(mwp)
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mwp), is.finite(psi_abs), !is.na(species))

# --- Settings you can tune ---
psi_min_p <- 0.99       # extreme quantile for Psi-min. 0.999 extrapolated up to 1.9 MPa past the
                        # data for species with ~30 obs and near-exponential tails (SALLEU, MALLAU)
min_tail  <- 5        # minimum tail points required to use EVT
pu_max    <- 0.95      # highest threshold prob
pu_min    <- 0.80      # lowest threshold prob (drop if needed for more tail points)

# --- Vector-safe POT quantile (no qgpd arg issues) ---
pot_quantile <- function(p, u, p_u, xi, beta) {
  if (p <= p_u) return(NA_real_)
  q <- (p - p_u) / (1 - p_u)
  q <- min(max(q, 0), 0.999999)

  if (!is.finite(xi) || !is.finite(beta) || beta <= 0) return(NA_real_)

  if (abs(xi) < 1e-12) {
    yq <- -beta * log(1 - q)               # xi -> 0 limit
  } else {
    yq <- (beta/xi) * ((1 - q)^(-xi) - 1)  # general case
  }
  u + yq
}

# --- 1) Adaptive threshold per species to try to reach min_tail ---
u_tbl <- dat %>%
  count(species, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    pu = pmin(pu_max, pmax(pu_min, 1 - (min_tail / n)))
  ) %>%
  left_join(dat %>% select(species, psi_abs), by = "species") %>%
  group_by(species, n, pu) %>%
  summarise(
    u = as.numeric(quantile(psi_abs, probs = unique(pu), na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- 2) Tail extraction + EVT fit (POT-GPD) ---
fits <- u_tbl %>%
  left_join(dat %>% select(species, psi_abs, mwp), by = "species") %>%
  group_by(species, n, pu, u) %>%
  summarise(
    x_tail = list(sort(psi_abs[psi_abs >= u])),
    k_tail = sum(psi_abs >= u),
    psi_min_obs = min(mwp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gpd_fit = map2(x_tail, u, ~{
      x <- unlist(.x)
      if (length(x) < min_tail) return(NULL)
      tryCatch(
        fExtremes::gpdFit(x, u = .y, type = "pwm"),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
    }),
    xi = map_dbl(gpd_fit, ~ if (is.null(.x)) NA_real_ else unname(.x@fit$par.ests["xi"])),
    beta = map_dbl(gpd_fit, ~ if (is.null(.x)) NA_real_ else unname(.x@fit$par.ests["beta"])),

    psi_min_evt_abs = pmap_dbl(list(u, pu, xi, beta), ~{
      if (any(!is.finite(c(..1, ..2, ..3, ..4))) || ..4 <= 0) return(NA_real_)
      pot_quantile(p = psi_min_p, u = ..1, p_u = ..2, xi = ..3, beta = ..4)
    }),
    # back to negative MPa; never less negative than the lowest observed value
    # (strongly bounded tails, e.g. ERIFAS xi = -1.4, can put the quantile inside the data)
    psi_min_evt = pmin(-psi_min_evt_abs, psi_min_obs),

    use_evt = is.finite(psi_min_evt) & (k_tail >= min_tail),
    psi_min_hybrid = if_else(use_evt, psi_min_evt, psi_min_obs),
    psi_min_method = if_else(use_evt, "EVT_POT_GPD", "Observed_min_lowN")) %>%
  select(species, n, pu, u, k_tail, xi, beta,
         psi_min_obs, psi_min_evt, psi_min_hybrid, psi_min_method)

# --- 3) Output table ---
print(fits %>% arrange(psi_min_method, k_tail))

write.csv(fits, here("output", "tables", "psi_min_by_species_hybrid.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Psi-min used by all downstream analyses (scripts 07, 08)
fits %>%
  select(species, psi_min = psi_min_hybrid, psi_min_method, psi_min_obs) %>%
  write_csv(here("data", "psi_min_by_species.csv"))

# shared x/y range so the panel is square
psi_lims <- range(c(fits$psi_min_obs, fits$psi_min_hybrid))

figSX_evt_ests <- ggplot() +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(data = fits,aes(y = psi_min_hybrid,
           x = psi_min_obs,
           shape = psi_min_method,
           color = species,
           ), size = 4) +
  coord_equal(xlim = psi_lims, ylim = psi_lims) +
  color_species +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(EVT_POT_GPD = 16, Observed_min_lowN = 17),
                     labels = c(EVT_POT_GPD = "EVT", Observed_min_lowN = "Observed (low n)")) +
  labs(x = "Observed Ψmin (MPa)", y = "Estimated Ψmin (MPa)",
       color = "Species", shape = "Method") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 15),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13))

figSX_evt_ests

ggsave(plot = figSX_evt_ests, here::here("output", "figures", "SI", "Fig_S05_evt_psi_min.jpg"), dpi = 600,
       height = 6,
       width = 8.5, units = "in")
```

#Figure S4 (Ψ distributions by species and study)

```{r}
# Stacked histograms of midday Ψ per species, filled by study (SEKI shown as Providence Creek)
site_cols <- c("Pepperwood" = "#E69F00", "Providence Creek" = "#56B4E9",
               "Sedgwick" = "#009E73", "Stunt Ranch" = "#CC79A7")  # Okabe-Ito

figS4_psi_dist <- df1 %>%
  mutate(site = recode(study, SEKI = "Providence Creek", StuntRanch = "Stunt Ranch"),
         site = factor(site, levels = names(site_cols))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mwp, fill = site)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, position = "stack", colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_cols, name = "Site") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = expression(Psi[MD]~"(MPa)"), y = "Count") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.key = element_blank())

figS4_psi_dist

ggsave(plot = figS4_psi_dist, here::here("output", "figures", "SI", "Fig_S04_psi_distributions.jpg"), dpi = 600,
       height = 8, width = 8, units = "in")
```

```{r}
#install.packages("devtools")

library(U.Taxonstand)  

SpCodes <- read_csv(here("data", "SpCodes.csv")) %>%
  mutate(species = SpCode6) %>% 
  mutate(family = familyMatch(splist = c(Genus), taxon = "plant")$family)

traits_df <- read_csv(here("data", "traits_rd_20250327.csv")) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(species = sp_code) %>% 
  select(species, functional_type, growth_form)

sp_info <- merge(traits_df, SpCodes) %>% 
  mutate(sp_code = SpCode6) %>% 
  mutate(dec_ever = leaf_habit_class(species)) %>%  # defined in 00_figure_setup.R
  mutate(growth_form = case_when(
    species %in% c("CERBET") ~ "tree/shrub",
    TRUE ~ as.character(growth_form)
  ))


sp_info %>% write_csv(here("data", "sp_info.csv"))
```


```{r}
table1_df <- merge(df1, sp_info, by = c("species")) %>%
```

#Q0: Conceptual Model:

#####Figure 2: (color)

```{r}
## conceptual model
# ---- x-axis standard mapping (-8 on left, 0 to the right) ----
xlim_mwp <- c(-8, 0)   

slp <- -0.198

ilfm.sat.vec <- seq(0.25, 1.25, length.out = 25)
MWPcrit <- numeric(length(ilfm.sat.vec))

for (i in seq_along(ilfm.sat.vec)) MWPcrit[i] <- solveForX(c(ilfm.sat.vec[i], slp), 1/0.7)
lfm.sat.vec <- 1 / ilfm.sat.vec
plot(MWPcrit, lfm.sat.vec, xlim = xlim_mwp, ylim = c(0,4),
     type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = expression(Psi[min]~"(MPa)"), ylab = "LFM @ MWP=0")

for (i in seq_along(ilfm.sat.vec)) MWPcrit[i] <- solveForX(c(ilfm.sat.vec[i], slp), 1/0.5)
lfm.sat.vec <- 1 / ilfm.sat.vec
lines(MWPcrit, lfm.sat.vec, lwd = 1)

for (i in seq_along(ilfm.sat.vec)) MWPcrit[i] <- solveForX(c(ilfm.sat.vec[i], slp), 1/1)
lfm.sat.vec <- 1 / ilfm.sat.vec
lines(MWPcrit, lfm.sat.vec, lwd = 1)

# conceptual figure, in standard space
lfm.sat <- c(0.9, 0.5)
slp <- -0.2
min.MWP <- c(-6, -3)

xy <- inversePlotData(c(min.MWP[1], 0), c(lfm.sat[1], slp))
head(xy)
plot(xy$MWP, xy$LFM, xlim = xlim_mwp)

(MWPcrit <- solveForX(c(lfm.sat[2], slp), 1/0.7))

#------
(max.iLFM <- lfm.sat + min.MWP * slp)
(min.LFM <- 1 / max.iLFM)

op <- par(mfrow = c(1,2))

plot(xlim_mwp, c(0,3), type = "n", xlab = "MWP", ylab = "1/LFM")
x <- list(); y <- list()
for (i in 1:2) {
  x[[i]] <- c(0, min.MWP[i])
  y[[i]] <- c(lfm.sat[i], max.iLFM[i])
  lines(x[[i]], y[[i]], type = "b", cex = 2, pch = c(1,19))
}

xy1 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[1]), c(lfm.sat[1], slp))
xy2 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[2]), c(lfm.sat[2], slp))
plot(xlim_mwp, c(0,3), type = "n", xlab = "MWP", ylab = "LFM")
lines(xy1$MWP, xy1$LFM, type = "l")
points(xy1[c(1,100), c("MWP","LFM")], cex = 2, pch = c(1,19))
lines(xy2$MWP, xy2$LFM, type = "l")
points(xy2[c(1,100), c("MWP","LFM")], cex = 2, pch = c(1,19))
par(op)

#-----
# Choose distinct colors for each line
cols <- c("steelblue3", "tomato3")  # i=1 -> cols[1], i=2 -> cols[2]

xy <- inversePlotData(c(min.MWP[1], 0), c(lfm.sat[1], slp))
plot(xy$MWP, xy$LFM, xlim = xlim_mwp)

(MWPcrit <- solveForX(c(lfm.sat[2], slp), 1/0.7))

(max.iLFM <- lfm.sat + min.MWP * slp)
(min.LFM  <- 1 / max.iLFM)

op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

## Panel 1: 1/LFM vs MWP
plot(xlim_mwp, c(0,3), type = "n", xlab = "MWP", ylab = "1/LFM")
mtext("A", side = 3, adj = 0, line = 1.2, font = 2, cex = 1.2)
x <- vector("list", 2)
y <- vector("list", 2)
for (i in 1:2) {
  x[[i]] <- c(0, min.MWP[i])
  y[[i]] <- c(lfm.sat[i], max.iLFM[i])
  lines(x[[i]], y[[i]], col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
  points(x[[i]][1], y[[i]][1], pch = 21, bg = "white", col = cols[i], cex = 2, lwd = 2)
  points(x[[i]][2], y[[i]][2], pch = 19, col = cols[i], cex = 2)
}

## Panel 2: LFM vs MWP
xy1 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[1]), c(lfm.sat[1], slp))
xy2 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[2]), c(lfm.sat[2], slp))
plot(xlim_mwp, c(0,3), type = "n", xlab = "MWP", ylab = "LFM")
mtext("B", side = 3, adj = 0, line = 1.2, font = 2, cex = 1.2)

lines(xy1$MWP, xy1$LFM, col = cols[1], lwd = 2)
points(xy1[1, c("MWP","LFM")],   pch = 21, bg = "white", col = cols[1], cex = 2, lwd = 2)
points(xy1[100, c("MWP","LFM")], pch = 19, col = cols[1], cex = 2)

lines(xy2$MWP, xy2$LFM, col = cols[2], lwd = 2)
points(xy2[1, c("MWP","LFM")],   pch = 21, bg = "white", col = cols[2], cex = 2, lwd = 2)
points(xy2[100, c("MWP","LFM")], pch = 19, col = cols[2], cex = 2)

par(op)

# ---- ggplot version: standard mapping ---------------------
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

cols <- c("steelblue3", "tomato3")
names(cols) <- c("1","2")

max.iLFM <- lfm.sat + min.MWP * slp

dfA_lines <- tibble(
  id = factor(c(1,1, 2,2)),
  MWP = c(0, min.MWP[1], 0, min.MWP[2]),
  invLFM = c(lfm.sat[1], max.iLFM[1], lfm.sat[2], max.iLFM[2])
)

dfA_open <- dfA_lines %>% group_by(id) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
dfA_filled <- dfA_lines %>% group_by(id) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()

xy1 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[1]), c(lfm.sat[1], slp)) %>% mutate(id = factor(1))
xy2 <- inversePlotData(c(0, min.MWP[2]), c(lfm.sat[2], slp)) %>% mutate(id = factor(2))
dfB_curve <- bind_rows(xy1, xy2)

dfB_open <- dfB_curve %>% group_by(id) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
dfB_filled <- dfB_curve %>% group_by(id) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()

axis_title_size <- 14
axis_text_size  <- 12

pt_size            <- 2.8
pt_alpha           <- 0.85
salvia_ring_size   <- 5
salvia_ring_stroke <- 0.5

# make legend slightly bigger

legend_text_size  <- 11
legend_key_h      <- unit(0.36, "cm")
legend_key_w      <- unit(1.2, "cm")  # longer so dashed is obvious

base_theme <- theme(
  plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
  axis.title = element_text(size = axis_title_size),
  axis.text  = element_text(size = axis_text_size),
  legend.title = element_text(size = legend_title_size),
  legend.text  = element_text(size = legend_text_size),
  legend.key.height = legend_key_h,
  legend.key.width  = legend_key_w
)

pA <- ggplot(dfB_curve, aes(x = MWP, y = LFM, color = id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +

           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 5) +

pB <- ggplot() +

            aes(x = MWP, y = invLFM, group = id, color = id), linewidth = 1) +
```

#Q1: Slopes and models

```{r}
# Model with untransformed LFM
mod <- glm(mwp ~ lfm, data = df1)
mod_summary <- summary(mod)

# Model with transformed LFM (inverse LFM)
mod_inv <- glm(mwp ~ ilfm, data = df1)
mod_inv_summary <- summary(mod_inv)

# Compare AIC and BIC
aic_values <- c(AIC(mod), AIC(mod_inv))
bic_values <- c(BIC(mod), BIC(mod_inv))
model_names <- c("Untransformed LFM", "Transformed LFM (iLFM)")

# Compute Pseudo R-squared (McFadden's R²)
pseudo_r2 <- function(model) {
  1 - (model$deviance / model$null.deviance)
}

r2_values <- c(pseudo_r2(mod), pseudo_r2(mod_inv))

# Compare residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  
plot(mod, main = "Untransformed LFM Model")
plot(mod_inv, main = "Transformed LFM Model")

# Create a summary table for comparison
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = model_names,
  AIC = aic_values,
  BIC = bic_values,
  Pseudo_R2 = r2_values
)

print(model_comparison)

# Determine the better model based on AIC
best_model <- ifelse(AIC(mod_inv) < AIC(mod), "Transformed LFM (iLFM)", "Untransformed LFM")
cat("Best model based on AIC:", best_model, "\n")
```

Study random effect: 
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)
library(performance)
#install.packages(c("pbkrtest", "lmerTest"))
library(lmerTest)
library(pbkrtest)

df1 <- df1 %>%
  mutate(
    species = as.factor(species),
    study   = as.factor(study),
    mwp     = as.numeric(mwp),
    ilfm    = as.numeric(ilfm)
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mwp), is.finite(ilfm)) %>%
  mutate(
    mwp_c = mwp - mean(mwp, na.rm = TRUE)   # center so intercepts are at mean mwp
  )

studies_per_species <- df1 %>%
  distinct(species, study) %>%
  count(species, name = "n_studies") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_studies))

print(studies_per_species)

n_by_species_study <- df1 %>%
  count(species, study, name = "n_obs") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_obs))

print(n_by_species_study)

write_csv(n_by_species_study, here("data", "study_species_n.csv"))

cat("\nSpecies with >1 study:",
    sum(studies_per_species$n_studies > 1),
    "out of", nrow(studies_per_species), "\n\n")

m_fe_lmer <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp_c * species, data = df1)
m_re      <- lmer(ilfm ~ mwp_c * species + (1 | study), data = df1, REML = FALSE)

aic_tab <- AIC(m_fe_lmer, m_re)
bic_tab <- BIC(m_fe_lmer, m_re)
print(aic_tab)
print(bic_tab)

delta_aic <- aic_tab$AIC[1] - aic_tab$AIC[2]
cat("\nDelta AIC (no RE minus RE) =", round(delta_aic, 2), "\n")

cat("\nVarCorr(m_re):\n")
print(VarCorr(m_re))
cat("\nIs singular?\n")
print(isSingular(m_re, tol = 1e-5))
cat("\nICC:\n")
print(performance::icc(m_re))

get_species_effects <- function(model, model_label) {

  ints <- emmeans(model, ~ species, at = list(mwp_c = 0)) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    transmute(
      species,
      component = "Intercept (at mean mwp)",
      estimate = emmean,
      se = SE,
      lo = lower.CL,
      hi = upper.CL,
      model = model_label
    )

  slps <- emtrends(model, ~ species, var = "mwp_c") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    transmute(
      species,
      component = "Slope (d ilfm / d mwp)",
      estimate = mwp_c.trend,
      se = SE,
      lo = lower.CL,
      hi = upper.CL,
      model = model_label
    )

  bind_rows(ints, slps)
}

effects_fe <- get_species_effects(m_fe_lmer, "No study RE")
effects_re <- get_species_effects(m_re,      "With study RE")

effects_all <- bind_rows(effects_fe, effects_re)

effects_wide <- effects_all %>%
  select(species, component, model, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = estimate) %>%
  mutate(
    diff = `With study RE` - `No study RE`,
    abs_diff = abs(diff)
  )

print(effects_wide %>% arrange(component, desc(abs_diff)) %>% head(30))

corr_slope <- effects_wide %>%
  filter(component == "Slope (d ilfm / d mwp)") %>%
  summarise(r = cor(`No study RE`, `With study RE`, use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  pull(r)

corr_int <- effects_wide %>%
  filter(component == "Intercept (at mean mwp)") %>%
  summarise(r = cor(`No study RE`, `With study RE`, use = "complete.obs")) %>%
  pull(r)

cat("\nCorrelation of species estimates (No RE vs With RE):\n",
    "  Intercepts r =", round(corr_int, 3), "\n",
    "  Slopes     r =", round(corr_slope, 3), "\n\n")

species_order <- effects_all %>%
  filter(component == "Slope (d ilfm / d mwp)", model == "With study RE") %>%
  arrange(estimate) %>%
  pull(species)

effects_plot <- effects_all %>%
  mutate(
    species = factor(as.character(species), levels = species_order),
    component = factor(component, levels = c("Intercept (at mean mwp)",
                                            "Slope (d ilfm / d mwp)")),
    model = factor(model, levels = c("No study RE", "With study RE"))
  )

p_compare <- ggplot(effects_plot,
                    aes(x = model, y = estimate, group = species)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.08, alpha = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Species-level estimate (± 95% CI)",
    title = "Sensitivity of species intercepts and slopes to adding a study random intercept"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

p_compare

ggsave(
  filename = here("output", "figures", "SI", "unused_study_RE_comparison.png"),
  plot     = p_compare,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 7,
  units    = "in",
  dpi      = 300
)
```

#Table S1: Mixed effects model results: 

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(here)

# Table S4: species intercepts (at the mean observed Psi) and slopes from the
# species-interaction linear model; Table S5 repeats them with a study random effect
mod_spp_int    <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp * species, data = df1)
mod_spp_int_re <- lmer(ilfm ~ mwp * species + (1 | study),
                      data = df1, REML = FALSE)

mwp_ref <- mean(df1$mwp, na.rm = TRUE)

species_params <- function(mod) {
  emm_int <- emmeans(mod, ~ species, at = list(mwp = mwp_ref)) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rename(
      intercept_iLFM     = emmean,
      intercept_iLFM_SE  = SE,
      intercept_iLFM_lwr = lower.CL,
      intercept_iLFM_upr = upper.CL
    ) %>%
    select(-df)

  emm_slp <- emtrends(mod, ~ species, var = "mwp") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rename(
      slope_iLFM     = mwp.trend,
      slope_iLFM_SE  = SE,
      slope_iLFM_lwr = lower.CL,
      slope_iLFM_upr = upper.CL
    ) %>%
    select(-df)

  emm_int %>%
    left_join(emm_slp, by = "species") %>%
    mutate(
      intercept_LFM = 100 * (1 / intercept_iLFM),
      mwp_ref = mwp_ref
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
}

table_species_params <- species_params(mod_spp_int)
write_csv(
  table_species_params,
  here("output", "tables", "Table_S04_species_params.csv")
)

table_study_re <- bind_rows(
  table_species_params %>% mutate(model = "lm: no study random effect"),
  species_params(mod_spp_int_re) %>% mutate(model = "lmer: study random effect")
)
write_csv(
  table_study_re,
  here("output", "tables", "Table_S05_study_random_effect.csv")
)

# HTML versions for the SI (same bootstrap style as Table S7; no pandoc needed)
save_param_html <- function(tab, file) {
  tab <- tab %>%
    transmute(Species = species, `Ref. MPa` = sprintf("%.3f", mwp_ref),
              `iLFM intercept` = sprintf("%.3f", intercept_iLFM), `int SE` = sprintf("%.3f", intercept_iLFM_SE),
              `int lower` = sprintf("%.3f", intercept_iLFM_lwr), `int upper` = sprintf("%.3f", intercept_iLFM_upr),
              slope = sprintf("%.3f", slope_iLFM), `slope SE` = sprintf("%.3f", slope_iLFM_SE),
              `slope lower` = sprintf("%.3f", slope_iLFM_lwr), `slope upper` = sprintf("%.3f", slope_iLFM_upr),
              `LFM intercept (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", intercept_LFM),
              across(any_of("model"), ~ .x, .names = "Model"))
  k <- knitr::kable(tab, format = "html", align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(tab) - 1))) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
  htmltools::save_html(
    htmltools::tagList(rmarkdown::html_dependency_jquery(), rmarkdown::html_dependency_bootstrap("simplex"),
                       htmltools::HTML(as.character(k))),
    file)
}
save_param_html(table_species_params, here("output", "tables", "Table_S04_species_params.html"))
save_param_html(table_study_re, here("output", "tables", "Table_S05_study_random_effect.html"))
```

#Concept dataframes:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(lme4)
library(broom.mixed)   
library(janitor)
library(readr)
library(here)


# Common-slope model (species intercepts, one slope); used for the Fig 5 isoclines and points.
# Fixed effects only, for the same reason as the species-interaction model below
mod_common_slope <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp + species, data = df1)

# Species intercepts and slopes from a fixed-effects species-interaction model (equivalent to a
# separate regression per species), so LFMmax = 1/intercept describes each species at the site(s)
# where it was sampled. With four unbalanced sites (two species at Sedgwick) a study random
# intercept is poorly identified and, when dropped from the extracted intercepts, shifts LFMmax
# (e.g. QUEDOU 205% -> 318%); the study random effect is kept as a sensitivity check (Table S5).
mod_species_interaction <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp * species, data = df1)

mod_species_study <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp * sp_site, data = df1)


extract_model_info <- function(model, model_name) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(model, effects = "fixed") %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
}

model_coeffs <- bind_rows(
  extract_model_info(mod_common_slope, "common_slope"),
  extract_model_info(mod_species_interaction, "species_interaction"),
  extract_model_info(mod_species_study, "species_site_interaction")
)

baseline_level <- function(var) levels(factor(var))[1]

get_fixef <- function(model) {
  if (inherits(model, "lmerMod")) return(lme4::fixef(model))
  return(stats::coef(model))
}

get_term <- function(beta, term1, term2 = NULL) {
  if (term1 %in% names(beta)) return(unname(beta[[term1]]))
  if (!is.null(term2) && term2 %in% names(beta)) return(unname(beta[[term2]]))
  return(0)
}

compute_group_terms <- function(model, group_var, model_type, slope_var = "mwp") {
  beta <- get_fixef(model)

  group_list <- unique(df1[[group_var]])
  base_group <- baseline_level(df1[[group_var]])

  map_dfr(group_list, function(grp) {

    intercept <- unname(beta[["(Intercept)"]])
    slope     <- unname(beta[[slope_var]])

    if (grp != base_group) {

      int_term <- paste0(group_var, grp)   
      intercept <- intercept + get_term(beta, int_term)

      slope_term1 <- paste0(slope_var, ":", group_var, grp)
      slope_term2 <- paste0(group_var, grp, ":", slope_var)
      slope <- slope + get_term(beta, slope_term1, slope_term2)
    }

    tibble(
      group = grp,
      intercept = intercept,
      slope = slope,
      model = model_type
    )
  })
}


coefs_common <- compute_group_terms(
  mod_common_slope, "species", "common_slope"
) %>% rename(species = group)

coefs_species_int <- compute_group_terms(
  mod_species_interaction, "species", "species_interaction"
) %>% rename(species = group)

coefs_species_study <- compute_group_terms(
  mod_species_study, "sp_site", "species_site_interaction"
) %>%
  rename(sp_study = group) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(sp_study, names = c("species", "study"), delim = "_")

coef_compare_df <- bind_rows(coefs_common, coefs_species_int, coefs_species_study) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    model == "species_interaction"         ~ "species",
    model == "common_slope"               ~ "grand",
    model == "species_site_interaction"    ~ "sp_study",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  select(-study)

range(coefs_species_int$slope, na.rm = TRUE)

concept_both_df <- merge(coef_compare_df, df1, by = c("species"), all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(model != "species_site_interaction") %>%
  merge(sp_info) %>%
  clean_names()

concept_study_df <- merge(coef_compare_df, df1, by = c("species"), all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(model == "species_site_interaction") %>%
  merge(sp_info) %>%
  clean_names()

concept_df_all <- bind_rows(concept_both_df, concept_study_df) %>%
  clean_names()

write_csv(concept_df_all, here::here("data", "concept_df.csv"))

concept_df <- concept_df_all %>%
  filter(group == "grand") %>%
  clean_names()
```

#####Figure S3 (post-hoc check: slope break near ΨTLP)

Nolan et al. (2020) proposed that the LFMC~Ψleaf relationship breaks into two segments at the turgor loss point (ΨTLP). Our primary model does not assume this breakpoint, but here we check for it directly: for each species with enough data spanning both sides of its independently measured ΨTLP (n >= 20, n >= 5 on each side), we fit a free-breakpoint segmented regression of ilfm ~ mwp (`segmented` package) and test for a significant change in slope (Davies' test). Species are colored where the slope break is significant (p < 0.05); the rest are shown in grey with a simple linear fit only.

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
library(segmented)

traits_tlp <- read_csv(here("data", "traits_rd_20250327.csv")) %>%
  clean_names()

d_tlp <- df1 %>%
  dplyr::select(species, study, date, mwp, lfm, ilfm) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mwp), is.finite(ilfm)) %>%
  left_join(traits_tlp %>% dplyr::select(species = sp_code, psi_tlp), by = "species") %>%
  filter(!is.na(psi_tlp)) %>%
  # Calocedrus decurrens (SEKI) was sampled in two campaigns with opposite-signed
  # mwp~ilfm slopes (2020-08/10: r = -0.69, expected direction; 2021-04/06: r = +0.47,
  # likely new-needle-flush phenology) that never overlap in mwp. Pooling both creates
  # a spurious "V"-shaped breakpoint at their boundary rather than a real TLP effect.
  # Restrict to the single, internally consistent 2020 campaign for this species; the
  # segmented fit is then close to (but not significantly different from) its ΨTLP
  # (breakpoint = -2.22 +/- 0.19 MPa vs. measured ΨTLP = -2.30 MPa; Davies p = 0.067),
  # i.e. no longer meets our p < 0.05 threshold, so it is grouped with the grey species below.
  filter(!(species == "CALDEC" & date >= as.Date("2021-01-01"))) %>%
  # Quercus douglasii was measured at both Pepperwood (n=12, Oct 2020/2021 + Jun 2022)
  # and Sedgwick (n=174, Mar-Sep 2022), and this species already shows a significant
  # site x slope interaction elsewhere in our analysis (Fig. S7/Table S5). Pooling both
  # sites shifts the breakpoint away from ΨTLP (-4.44 MPa vs. measured -3.40 MPa); using
  # Sedgwick alone (a single, internally consistent site/season with 174 points spanning
  # both sides of ΨTLP) brings the breakpoint closer to ΨTLP (-3.93 +/- 0.21 MPa) while the
  # slope break remains highly significant (Davies p = 0.0027, vs. p < 0.001 pooled) -
  # i.e., unlike C. decurrens, this is a real signal whose location the site pooling was
  # distorting, not a spurious artifact.
  filter(!(species == "QUEDOU" & study == "Pepperwood"))

sp_list_tlp <- d_tlp %>% count(species, psi_tlp) %>% filter(n >= 20) %>% pull(species)

fit_one_tlp <- function(sp) {
  dsp <- d_tlp %>% filter(species == sp)
  tlp <- unique(dsp$psi_tlp)[1]
  if (sum(dsp$mwp < tlp) < 5 || sum(dsp$mwp >= tlp) < 5) return(NULL)

  lm0 <- lm(ilfm ~ mwp, data = dsp)
  seg_free <- tryCatch(segmented(lm0, seg.Z = ~mwp, psi = tlp), error = function(e) NULL)
  davies <- tryCatch(davies.test(lm0, ~mwp), error = function(e) NULL)
  p_val <- if (!is.null(davies)) davies$p.value else NA_real_
  sig <- isTRUE(!is.na(p_val) && p_val < 0.05 && !is.null(seg_free))

  mwp_seq <- seq(min(dsp$mwp), max(dsp$mwp), length.out = 200)
  if (sig) {
    pred <- as.numeric(predict(seg_free, newdata = data.frame(mwp = mwp_seq)))
    bp <- unname(seg_free$psi[1, "Est."])
  } else {
    pred <- as.numeric(predict(lm0, newdata = data.frame(mwp = mwp_seq)))
    bp <- NA_real_
  }

  list(
    points = dsp,
    line = tibble(species = sp, mwp = mwp_seq, ilfm_pred = pred),
    summary = tibble(species = sp, psi_tlp = tlp, n = nrow(dsp),
                      davies_p = p_val, breakpoint = bp, significant = sig)
  )
}

fits_tlp <- purrr::compact(purrr::map(sp_list_tlp, fit_one_tlp))

points_df_tlp  <- purrr::map_dfr(fits_tlp, "points")
lines_df_tlp   <- purrr::map_dfr(fits_tlp, "line")
summary_df_tlp <- purrr::map_dfr(fits_tlp, "summary")

write_csv(summary_df_tlp, here("output", "tables", "SI_Fig13_tlp_breakpoint_summary.csv"))

sp_label_vec_tlp <- setNames(str_replace(sp_info$Genus_species, " ", "\n"), sp_info$species)
sp_order_tlp <- summary_df_tlp %>% arrange(desc(significant), species) %>% pull(species)

points_df_tlp <- points_df_tlp %>%
  left_join(summary_df_tlp %>% dplyr::select(species, significant), by = "species") %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = sp_order_tlp),
         ilfm_obs = 1 / lfm)
lines_df_tlp <- lines_df_tlp %>%
  left_join(summary_df_tlp %>% dplyr::select(species, significant), by = "species") %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = sp_order_tlp),
         )
summary_df_tlp <- summary_df_tlp %>% mutate(species = factor(species, levels = sp_order_tlp))

# Breakpoint/TLP markers on the MPa axis (plotted in model space, iLFM ~ mwp, so fits are straight)
vline_df_tlp <- summary_df_tlp %>%
  filter(significant) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, breakpoint, psi_tlp) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(breakpoint, psi_tlp), names_to = "type", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(type = recode(type,
                        breakpoint = "Estimated breakpoint",
                        psi_tlp = "ΨTLP"))

n_sig_tlp <- sum(summary_df_tlp$significant)
n_nonsig_tlp <- sum(!summary_df_tlp$significant)
cat(n_sig_tlp, "of", nrow(summary_df_tlp), "species show a significant slope break (Davies p < 0.05);",
    n_nonsig_tlp, "do not.\n")

figS13_tlp <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = points_df_tlp %>% filter(!significant),
             aes(x = mwp, y = ilfm_obs), color = "grey65", alpha = 0.5, size = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = lines_df_tlp %>% filter(!significant),
            aes(x = mwp, y = ilfm_pred), color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = points_df_tlp %>% filter(significant),
             aes(x = mwp, y = ilfm_obs, color = species), alpha = 0.7, size = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = lines_df_tlp %>% filter(significant),
            aes(x = mwp, y = ilfm_pred, color = species), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = vline_df_tlp, aes(xintercept = value, linetype = type),
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  color_species +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Estimated breakpoint" = "dashed",
                                    "ΨTLP" = "dotted")) +
  # tick spacing scales with each panel's Ψ range so labels never collide
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(lim) {
    w <- if (diff(lim) > 5) 2 else if (diff(lim) > 1.8) 1 else 0.5
    seq(ceiling(lim[1] / w) * w, lim[2], by = w)
  }) +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free", ncol = 6,
             labeller = as_labeller(sp_label_vec_tlp)) +
  labs(x = expression(Psi[MD]~"(MPa)"), y = "iLFM (1/LFM)", linetype = NULL) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "italic", size = 14),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 18))

figS13_tlp

ggsave(plot = figS13_tlp,
       filename = here::here("output", "figures", "SI", "Fig_S03_tlp_breakpoints.jpg"),
       dpi = 600, width = 13, height = 9, units = "in")
```

Figure S3. Post-hoc test for a slope break in the iLFM ~ ΨMD relationship near the turgor loss point (ΨTLP), following the logic of Nolan et al. (2020). Top row (colored): the seven species (of 18 with sufficient data spanning both sides of ΨTLP) with a statistically significant change in slope (Davies' test, p < 0.05); dashed vertical line = breakpoint estimated by free-knot segmented regression, dotted vertical line = independently measured ΨTLP (`data/traits_rd_20250327.csv`). Remaining panels (grey): the eleven species with no significant slope break, shown with a single linear fit. Seven additional species in the dataset had insufficient data spanning both sides of ΨTLP and are excluded. For *Calocedrus decurrens*, the panel shown uses only its 2020 (Aug-Oct) field campaign: pooling with a second 2021 (Apr-Jun) campaign produced a spurious, highly significant "V"-shaped breakpoint driven by the two campaigns having opposite-signed ΨMD~iLFM slopes (likely a new-needle-flush phenology effect in the spring campaign), not a TLP-associated transition. Restricted to the single consistent campaign, its estimated breakpoint (-2.22 +/- 0.19 MPa) falls close to its measured ΨTLP (-2.30 MPa) but the change in slope is not significant at this reduced sample size (n = 36, Davies p = 0.067), so it is retained here in the grey (non-significant) group. For *Quercus douglasii*, the panel shown excludes a small (n = 12), site-mismatched Pepperwood subsample and uses only its larger Sedgwick dataset (n = 174, a single site/season, Mar-Sep 2022); this species already shows a significant site x slope interaction elsewhere in our analysis (Fig. S7/Table S5). Unlike C. decurrens, this correction did not remove the signal: the slope break remains highly significant (Davies p = 0.0027) and its breakpoint moves closer to the measured ΨTLP (-3.93 +/- 0.21 MPa vs. -3.40 MPa, compared to -4.44 MPa when both sites are pooled), indicating that site-pooling was distorting rather than creating this breakpoint.
